pathway.title: Excelerate Energy, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The business profile is adequate, anchored on contracts rather than scale: terminal services were 45.70% of nine-month 2026 revenue and remaining performance obligations were USD 18,329.6 million at 2026-09-30. At the 2025 year-end terminal charters held minimum contracted cash flows of USD 3,315.2 million over a weighted average 5.8 years, against USD 17,031.2 million for LNG, gas and power contracts, which are 83.71% of the combined USD 20,346.4 million. Most long-dated contract value is therefore gas supply with commodity pass-through and counterparty exposure, so headline visibility overstates the protected terminal income. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation F06; calculation C10

- Leverage is moderate and has risen from net cash: total debt was 2.28x last-twelve-months EBITDA and net debt 1.53x at 2026-09-30, or 1.55x pro forma for the payment due 2026-12-03. On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the figures are lower, so the choice of EBITDA does not change the conclusion. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F01; calculation F02

- Cash generation is the weak point, not earnings: nine-month free cash flow was negative USD 59.10 million because growth spending of about USD 286.69 million outran operating cash flow, which itself fell 28.68% on collection and payment timing in LNG sales and higher interest on the notes. Operating cash flow still exceeded maintenance capital spending by USD 220.92 million, and the final payment of about USD 210 million on the Excelerate Acadia terminal is complete, but the carrier balance and conversion contract that follow have no stated cost. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation F04; calculation C01; calculation C09; calculation C13

- Liquidity is adequate: cash plus the undrawn revolver was USD 856.74 million at 2026-09-30, before the dividend and distribution of USD 10.30 million payable on 2026-12-03 and the October 2026 events, with the revolver undrawn and maturing in March 2029. The refinancing risk is concentrated in time rather than near: 74.24% of principal at the 2025 year-end falls due in 2030, mostly the unsecured notes. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F01; calculation F05; calculation C04

- Counterparty and deployment risks are the main earnings risks: four customers took 50% of nine-month revenue, partly because some buy large LNG and gas volumes, the Iraq start moved to the second quarter of 2027 and a supply force majeure notice is outstanding. The new Iraq-related cash flows are therefore later than the annual report indicated. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation F07

- Structure and control weaken creditor protection: the unsecured notes of USD 800 million rank behind a USD 500 million secured revolver and USD 288.47 million of financings secured on specific assets (USD 788.47 million if the revolver were drawn in full), a holder controlling 72.5% of the votes receives tax receivable agreement payments, and a seventh credit agreement amendment is undescribed, so covenant headroom is not established even though the issuer states it complied with its covenants at 2026-09-30. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C05; calculation F08

cells.text: Owns and operates LNG and natural gas infrastructure: at 2026-09-30 it controlled or operated 12 floating regasification terminals, one onshore regasification terminal, two LNG carriers and a combined heat and power plant, with a regional presence in 15 countries.
Asset base is mobile and redeployable, which supports recovery of value but exposes earnings to redeployment gaps.

Fixed daily-rate take-or-pay time charters with inflation escalators; customers generally bear fuel, port fees and LNG boil-off; contracts can end on material breach, change in law or extended force majeure, and some customers hold early termination rights with fees.
Stable cash flow, with termination triggers that matter most in disrupted markets.

Sells LNG, natural gas, power and steam under long-term supply agreements; the company says sourced LNG is primarily sold on a back-to-back price basis. Includes the Petrobangla supply agreement (0.85 MTPA in 2026 and 2027, then 1.0 MTPA to 2040) and the Jamaica business acquired in May 2025.
Revenue is large but largely pass-through; margin, not revenue, supports debt service.

Minimum contracted cash flows at 2025-12-31: USD 3,315.2 million for terminal services (5.8 years weighted average remaining term) and USD 17,031.2 million for LNG, gas and power (9.3 years). Remaining performance obligations were USD 18,329.6 million at 2026-09-30, measured with commodity futures prices.
Visibility is long, but most of it is gas supply value that depends on commodity pricing and counterparties.

A mix of state-owned energy companies, transmission operators and industrial users; contracts with customers in Argentina, Brazil, Bangladesh, Finland, Germany, Iraq, Pakistan and the UAE for terminal services, and in Bangladesh, Iraq, Jamaica and the United States for LNG, gas and power. Four customers each took at least 10% of nine-month 2026 revenue.
Nine-month 2026 revenue by region: North America including the Caribbean 41.30%, Asia Pacific 20.45%, Latin America 15.38%, Middle East 13.40%, Europe 8.24%, other 1.23%.
Single-country exposure to Jamaica after the acquisition; about 18% of fixed assets are in Jamaica.

Long-term LNG purchase agreements include QatarEnergy (15 years from 2026, under force majeure notice since March 2026), Venture Global (20 years, dependent on a plant not expected to operate within 12 months at 2025-12-31) and a Jamaica agreement assumed with the acquisition. Purchase and capacity obligations are USD 750.3 million within twelve months.
Take-or-pay purchase obligations create cash calls if resale contracts are interrupted.
Management describes itself as the global leader in offshore regasification capacity and cites competition from other floating terminal owners, LNG sellers and LNG-to-power developers.
Management Language; position is not independently evidenced in the filings.
Operations depend on seafarers on board the terminals and on local port, pipeline and power infrastructure in each market; most long-lived assets are outside the United States.
Operational and country risk is spread across many markets but single-site outages interrupt a contract.

runs.text: Strengths, ranked. First, long-term take-or-pay terminal and supply contracts: remaining performance obligations of USD 18,329.6 million and a 5.8-year weighted average remaining terminal term give visible cash flow, which supports debt service and refinancing confidence. Second, moderate leverage with an equity cushion: 2.28x total and 1.53x net against earnings, with new equity funding part of the Jamaica purchase, which limits the leverage increase. Third, adequate liquidity: USD 856.74 million of cash and undrawn revolver with no maturity before 2029 beyond scheduled amortisation, which gives time to execute the growth plan. Fourth, a redeployable fleet of 12 floating regasification terminals, one onshore terminal and two LNG carriers at 2026-09-30, which lets a terminal move to a new contract, as Excelerate Acadia did to Jordan, and supports recovery value. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation F01; calculation F02; calculation F05; calculation F06

Weaknesses, ranked. First, negative free cash flow in 2026 from growth spending, which drains cash and makes liquidity depend on the revolver. Second, concentrated, state-linked customers: four took 50% of revenue, so one payment failure would hit income and the revolver's tests. Third, deployment and supply risk from the Gulf conflict: the Iraq start moved to the second quarter of 2027, which delays new earnings while capital is already committed. Fourth, structural subordination and weak protections: unsecured notes behind secured debt, control by one holder and an undescribed seventh amendment. Fifth, a 2030 maturity concentration of 74.24% of principal, which makes refinancing market-dependent in one year. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation F04; calculation F07

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The defining transaction is the purchase of New Fortress Energy's Jamaica business, which closed on 2025-05-14. The initial cash price of USD 1,055.2 million fell by about USD 28.7 million after adjustments for cash, debt, expenses, working capital and inventory to USD 1,026.5 million, buying the Montego Bay and Old Harbour LNG terminals and the Clarendon power plant. The company recorded goodwill of about USD 235.0 million and customer-relationship intangibles of USD 369.0 million, and the business contributed USD 262.5 million of revenue and USD 53.9 million of net income from the closing date to year-end 2025. The company printed pro forma 2025 revenue of USD 1,376.5 million and net income of USD 201.7 million, as if the purchase and its funding had occurred on 2024-01-01. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 148–149; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; calculation C05

The new debt was one issue: the operating partnership's USD 800 million of senior unsecured notes due May 2030, issued at par under an indenture dated 2025-05-05 and guaranteed by certain direct and indirect restricted subsidiaries. Interest is paid each May and November. The proceeds, with USD 201.8 million of net equity proceeds from 8,000,000 new Class A shares and cash on hand, paid for the acquisition, repaid the term loan in full and covered fees. Alongside it the revolver was amended three times in 2025: the Fourth Amendment on 2025-03-26 added acquisition and debt baskets and a broader collateral maintenance covenant, the Fifth on 2025-04-21 extended maturity to March 2029 and raised commitments to USD 500.0 million, and the Sixth on 2025-09-26 gave more flexibility for investments and restricted payments. A Seventh Amendment dated 2025-12-31 is listed as an exhibit to the annual report but not described. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 103–105; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 155–157; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19

No new debt was raised in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Instead the company signed growth commitments that will need funding: the acquisition of an LNG carrier in July 2026 for a first floating storage and regasification conversion, with a ten percent downpayment in the third quarter and the remainder due in the first quarter of 2027; a conversion contract awarded to Seatrium in October 2026; and a share repurchase program of up to USD 75.0 million approved in December 2025, under which USD 36.246 million of authorisation remained at 2026-09-30. Neither the carrier price nor the conversion contract value is stated, so the borrowing need for 2027 is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ee-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54

fields.value: Covenants are printed only as of year-end 2025 and no issuer-reported ratio or headroom is given for any date. The revolver requires a maximum consolidated total leverage of 3.50x, rising to 4.25x when aggregate unsecured debt is USD 250.0 million or more (on the filing's wording the higher level applies while the unsecured 2030 notes are outstanding), a minimum consolidated interest coverage of 2.50x, and collateral coverage of at least the greater of USD 750.0 million and 130% of credit exposure; the March 2025 amendment broadened the collateral test. The Experience financing requires minimum equity of 500.0, a maximum debt-to-equity ratio of 3.5 to 1 and minimum cash and availability of 20.0, and the Bangladesh loans a quarterly project debt service cover of at least 1.10. The issuer states compliance with all covenants at 2026-09-30. The covenant definitions differ from the metrics computed here, so no headroom is calculated.

fields.value: The nine months brought no new borrowing and show repayments of long-term debt of 17.323 and related-party debt of 7.792, share repurchases of 10.4 in the third quarter (291,157 shares at a weighted average price of 35.21 dollars), and a dividend of 0.09 dollars per Class A share declared on 2026-10-29. The Jamaica arbitration concluded in September 2026 with an award of 36.340 inclusive of interest and fees, retained by the seller and secured by escrow, and paid in October 2026. In March 2026 a force majeure notice was received from QatarEnergy and passed on under the supply agreement with Petrobangla. The new terminal, Excelerate Acadia, was delivered in the second quarter of 2026 for a final milestone payment of about 210, and began a nine-month charter in Jordan in July 2026. Contracts were signed in 2026 for Colombia (seven years from the first quarter of 2027), a five-year Sequoia extension through 2038 and the Bahamas hub, and the Seatrium conversion contract was awarded in October 2026 with no value stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A downside sequence the filings support begins with a force majeure or shipping disruption that interrupts purchased LNG supply, which the issuer already faces on its Qatar purchase agreement and passes on to Petrobangla under its long-term supply agreement. A first break would show in LNG, gas and power margins and operating cash flow, followed by lower EBITDA and thinner cash against the rising capital programme and shareholder payments; the observable tests are quarterly operating cash flow, the revolver availability and the year-end covenant disclosure. No numerical stress is established here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance fact pack for Excelerate Energy, Inc. (issuer ee-1888447) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot (full credit assessment) pathway. Scope is the business, operating model, ownership and control, governance, financing transactions and dated events in the five supplied filings. No rating, valuation or recommendation is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Excelerate is a contracted LNG-terminal and gas-supply business whose credit strength rests on long-term take-or-pay income from a mix of state-owned, utility and industrial customers, so creditors should weigh counterparty, concentration and deployment risk, and the control held by one shareholder, above scale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The contracted base is real but moving: the Iraq terminal start has slipped from the third quarter of 2026 to the second quarter of 2027, four customers took 50% of nine-month revenue, and one holder controls 72.5% of the voting power. Contract expiries, executed debt documents and board composition are not supplied, so legal protection and renewal risk are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Contracted terminal income is the credit anchor but not the majority of revenue: terminal services were 45.70% of nine-month 2026 revenue and the rest was LNG, gas and power sales, which pass most commodity cost through and carry a thinner margin, since the cost of LNG, gas and power equalled 81.59% of those sales. Minimum contracted cash flows at the 2025 year-end were USD 3,315.2 million for terminal services with a weighted average remaining term of 5.8 years, and USD 17,031.2 million for LNG, gas and power with 9.3 years.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Counterparty and concentration risk is the main revenue risk, because four customers each took at least 10% and together 50% of nine-month 2026 revenue, and the largest alone took 16%. Customers include state-owned energy companies in emerging markets, so credit support depends on sovereign-linked payment performance; the filings report no write-down of trade receivables on lease or time charter services in the nine months of 2026 or 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control sits with one shareholder and the company is a controlled company relying on exemptions from independence requirements: a holding company controlled by Kaiser owns all Class B shares and 72.5% of the combined voting power, and also receives payments under a tax receivable agreement. Distributions to public and Class B holders are pro rata, but the revolver permits general distributions only while liquidity is at least USD 200.0 million and leverage is at most 3.25x, with separate baskets for tax, tax receivable agreement and overhead payments, and no sponsor extraction beyond pro rata payouts is documented.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2025 Jamaica acquisition changed the risk profile: it cost USD 1,026.5 million after adjustments, was funded by USD 800 million of senior unsecured notes due 2030, USD 201.8 million of new equity and cash on hand, and added the Jamaica gas and power business, so North America including the Caribbean is now 41.30% of revenue by region. Equity covered a minority of the price, so the purchase raised debt, and the sources and uses of funds are not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Deployment is the live operating risk: the Gulf conflict moved the Iraq start from the third quarter of 2026 to the second quarter of 2027, forced a force majeure exchange with Qatari and Bangladeshi counterparties, redirected the new terminal to a nine-month Jordan charter, and changed the Colombia plan from redeploying one terminal to using other terminals outside the Gulf. Earnings now depend on redeploying assets on schedule, not only on contracts already signed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but incomplete for legal protection: statements are audited and quarterly, yet the covenant terms are summarised only, contract expiry dates by terminal are not in the extracted text, and a seventh credit agreement amendment dated 2025-12-31 is listed as an exhibit without any description.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a cautious reading is the size and tenor of contracted revenue: remaining performance obligations on long-term customer arrangements were USD 18,329.6 million at 2026-09-30, terminal customers carry most operating costs, management says contracts are regularly amended and extended, and the filings report no write-downs of lease or time charter receivables in the nine months of 2026 or 2025. The controlling holder has also supported obligations, giving an uncapped construction and operating guarantee for a deepwater port and a letter of credit for its decommissioning, and no dividend recapitalisation, priming or creditor exchange appears in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if executed debt documents showed tight limits on distributions and asset transfers, a contract schedule showed most terminal charters running well beyond the 2029 revolver maturity, and the Iraq and Colombia terminals started on the revised dates. It would worsen if a state customer delayed payment, force majeure turned into termination, or leverage moved toward the 3.25x level at which general distributions stop being permitted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The defining transaction is the purchase of New Fortress Energy's Jamaica business, which closed on 2025-05-14. The initial cash price of USD 1,055.2 million fell by about USD 28.7 million after adjustments for cash, debt, expenses, working capital and inventory to USD 1,026.5 million, buying the Montego Bay and Old Harbour LNG terminals and the Clarendon power plant. The company recorded goodwill of about USD 235.0 million and customer-relationship intangibles of USD 369.0 million, and the business contributed USD 262.5 million of revenue and USD 53.9 million of net income from the closing date to year-end 2025. The company printed pro forma 2025 revenue of USD 1,376.5 million and net income of USD 201.7 million, as if the purchase and its funding had occurred on 2024-01-01.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The new debt was one issue: the operating partnership's USD 800 million of senior unsecured notes due May 2030, issued at par under an indenture dated 2025-05-05 and guaranteed by certain direct and indirect restricted subsidiaries. Interest is paid each May and November. The proceeds, with USD 201.8 million of net equity proceeds from 8,000,000 new Class A shares and cash on hand, paid for the acquisition, repaid the term loan in full and covered fees. Alongside it the revolver was amended three times in 2025: the Fourth Amendment on 2025-03-26 added acquisition and debt baskets and a broader collateral maintenance covenant, the Fifth on 2025-04-21 extended maturity to March 2029 and raised commitments to USD 500.0 million, and the Sixth on 2025-09-26 gave more flexibility for investments and restricted payments. A Seventh Amendment dated 2025-12-31 is listed as an exhibit to the annual report but not described.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new debt was raised in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Instead the company signed growth commitments that will need funding: the acquisition of an LNG carrier in July 2026 for a first floating storage and regasification conversion, with a ten percent downpayment in the third quarter and the remainder due in the first quarter of 2027; a conversion contract awarded to Seatrium in October 2026; and a share repurchase program of up to USD 75.0 million approved in December 2025, under which USD 36.246 million of authorisation remained at 2026-09-30. Neither the carrier price nor the conversion contract value is stated, so the borrowing need for 2027 is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Sponsor / Governance Risk Level is Medium. The level is driven by concentrated control with controlled-company exemptions and payments to the controlling holder under the tax receivable agreement, because they reduce outside oversight and create cash claims ahead of creditors, which implies moderate leakage and monitoring risk for lenders. Countervailing evidence is that distributions are pro rata and gated by leverage and liquidity tests, equity funded part of the acquisition, and no extraction, priming or creditor exchange is documented. Further analysis requires the executed debt documents, the stockholder's agreement and board information.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment of Excelerate Energy, Inc. (issuer ee-1888447) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot (full credit assessment) pathway. Scope is the business profile, financial profile, outlook, downside, ranked drivers and monitoring triggers drawn from the supplied filings and the three earlier analyses. No rating, relative-value view or sizing is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Excelerate's credit is adequate: contracted take-or-pay income and moderate leverage support debt service, but negative 2026 free cash flow, concentrated state-linked customers and delayed deployments leave creditors reliant on the undrawn revolver and unproven covenant headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was 1.53x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-30, or 1.55x pro forma for the dividend and distribution payable on 2026-12-03, and EBITDA covered cash interest 4.45x. Free cash flow was negative USD 59.10 million in the nine months, but operating cash flow still exceeded maintenance capital spending by USD 220.92 million, so the weakness is growth spending, not core earnings, and the next growth costs are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F01; calculation F03; calculation F04; calculation C01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business profile is adequate, anchored on contracts rather than scale: terminal services were 45.70% of nine-month 2026 revenue and remaining performance obligations were USD 18,329.6 million at 2026-09-30. At the 2025 year-end terminal charters held minimum contracted cash flows of USD 3,315.2 million over a weighted average 5.8 years, against USD 17,031.2 million for LNG, gas and power contracts, which are 83.71% of the combined USD 20,346.4 million. Most long-dated contract value is therefore gas supply with commodity pass-through and counterparty exposure, so headline visibility overstates the protected terminal income.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation F06; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is moderate and has risen from net cash: total debt was 2.28x last-twelve-months EBITDA and net debt 1.53x at 2026-09-30, or 1.55x pro forma for the payment due 2026-12-03. On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the figures are lower, so the choice of EBITDA does not change the conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F01; calculation F02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash generation is the weak point, not earnings: nine-month free cash flow was negative USD 59.10 million because growth spending of about USD 286.69 million outran operating cash flow, which itself fell 28.68% on collection and payment timing in LNG sales and higher interest on the notes. Operating cash flow still exceeded maintenance capital spending by USD 220.92 million, and the final payment of about USD 210 million on the Excelerate Acadia terminal is complete, but the carrier balance and conversion contract that follow have no stated cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation F04; calculation C01; calculation C09; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is adequate: cash plus the undrawn revolver was USD 856.74 million at 2026-09-30, before the dividend and distribution of USD 10.30 million payable on 2026-12-03 and the October 2026 events, with the revolver undrawn and maturing in March 2029. The refinancing risk is concentrated in time rather than near: 74.24% of principal at the 2025 year-end falls due in 2030, mostly the unsecured notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F01; calculation F05; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Counterparty and deployment risks are the main earnings risks: four customers took 50% of nine-month revenue, partly because some buy large LNG and gas volumes, the Iraq start moved to the second quarter of 2027 and a supply force majeure notice is outstanding. The new Iraq-related cash flows are therefore later than the annual report indicated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation F07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Structure and control weaken creditor protection: the unsecured notes of USD 800 million rank behind a USD 500 million secured revolver and USD 288.47 million of financings secured on specific assets (USD 788.47 million if the revolver were drawn in full), a holder controlling 72.5% of the votes receives tax receivable agreement payments, and a seventh credit agreement amendment is undescribed, so covenant headroom is not established even though the issuer states it complied with its covenants at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C05; calculation F08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a more favourable view is that the cash weakness reflects growth timing: operating cash flow exceeded maintenance capital spending by USD 220.92 million over nine months and by USD 312.40 million over twelve months, most capital spending is growth, many older contracts have been extended, the issuer states covenant compliance and none of the debt matures before 2029 apart from scheduled amortisation. If the Iraq, Colombia and conversion projects deliver contracted earnings on time, leverage should fall from 1.53x without new borrowing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a weaker view is that protections cannot be verified: covenant levels are dated, an amendment is undescribed, customers are concentrated and sovereign-linked, and the carrier and conversion costs are unknown. The view would improve with executed documents showing wide headroom against a 3.25x distribution gate and the revolver tests, a contract schedule with long remaining terms, and on-time starts for Iraq and Colombia. It would worsen if the Iraq start slipped again, a state customer paid late, force majeure became termination, or free cash flow stayed negative after growth spending eased.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths, ranked. First, long-term take-or-pay terminal and supply contracts: remaining performance obligations of USD 18,329.6 million and a 5.8-year weighted average remaining terminal term give visible cash flow, which supports debt service and refinancing confidence. Second, moderate leverage with an equity cushion: 2.28x total and 1.53x net against earnings, with new equity funding part of the Jamaica purchase, which limits the leverage increase. Third, adequate liquidity: USD 856.74 million of cash and undrawn revolver with no maturity before 2029 beyond scheduled amortisation, which gives time to execute the growth plan. Fourth, a redeployable fleet of 12 floating regasification terminals, one onshore terminal and two LNG carriers at 2026-09-30, which lets a terminal move to a new contract, as Excelerate Acadia did to Jordan, and supports recovery value.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation F01; calculation F02; calculation F05; calculation F06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses, ranked. First, negative free cash flow in 2026 from growth spending, which drains cash and makes liquidity depend on the revolver. Second, concentrated, state-linked customers: four took 50% of revenue, so one payment failure would hit income and the revolver's tests. Third, deployment and supply risk from the Gulf conflict: the Iraq start moved to the second quarter of 2027, which delays new earnings while capital is already committed. Fourth, structural subordination and weak protections: unsecured notes behind secured debt, control by one holder and an undescribed seventh amendment. Fifth, a 2030 maturity concentration of 74.24% of principal, which makes refinancing market-dependent in one year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation F04; calculation F07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Excelerate owns and operates floating regasification terminals, an onshore terminal, LNG carriers and a combined heat and power plant, and sells LNG, gas and power. Its history of acquisition is short: a public listing in 2022, the purchase of the Sequoia terminal in 2023 and the Jamaica business in 2025. Visibility comes from fixed-rate take-or-pay charters under which customers generally bear fuel, port fees and boil-off, which supports debt service, but contracts can end on breach, change in law or extended force majeure, so visibility is conditional. Concentration is high and cyclicality sits in the LNG, gas and power line, which was 54.30% of nine-month revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation F06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The registrant is a holding company with a controlling interest in the operating partnership, which borrows and issues the notes; 72.5% of the votes and of the partnership interests sit with a holder controlled by Kaiser. This is a controlled company relying on exemptions, with pro rata distributions, tax receivable agreement payments and a related-party sale-leaseback financing. Financial policy is moderate on evidence: payouts of USD 76.40 million in nine months (buybacks, dividends and distributions) sit within revolver restricted-payment limits of leverage at most 3.25x with liquidity of at least USD 200.0 million, or up to 3.0% of equity value a year, although the capacity used is not shown, and no dividend recapitalisation, priming or creditor exchange appears in the filings; the Sponsor and governance risk level from the earlier analysis is Medium. The creditor risk is leakage capacity, not demonstrated leakage, and the notes are guaranteed only by certain restricted subsidiaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; calculation F08; calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring in terminals and cyclical and concentrated in gas supply. Terminal charters are fixed-rate with escalators, customers generally bear fuel and port costs, many older contracts have already been extended and all owned floating terminals were contracted at 2025-12-31, so terminal income is predictable but terminable on stated events. LNG, gas and power revenue follows commodity prices and a few customers, and Qatar supply is under force majeure. Credit linkage: contracted income supports debt service as long as counterparties pay, while pass-through revenue inflates the denominator of any revenue-based ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 129.3 million to USD 133.5 million between the third quarters (about 3.21%) even though LNG, gas and power revenue fell on fewer short-term sales and the timing of deliveries under the Atlantic Basin agreement, which cost USD 11.0 million, because the Jordan charter (USD 13.9 million) and short-term LNG opportunities (USD 6.1 million) more than offset it. Terminal margins are shielded from fuel and port costs that customers generally bear; LNG margins depend on back-to-back pricing that the issuer describes but the filings do not quantify. Business development costs rose by USD 3.4 million, so margins can be defended against volume timing but not shown to be defended against a protracted supply interruption.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Last-twelve-months operating cash flow was almost the same as capital spending (1.03x), so free cash flow was thin, while maintenance spending was small: 33.585 of 320.278 gross in nine months (10.49%). Cash interest paid took 22.46% of last-twelve-months EBITDA, and the notes' annual coupon of USD 64.0 million is paid in May and November. Capex flexibility is real because most spending is growth and the largest 2026 outflow, the Acadia milestone, is complete, but projects with signed contracts (Iraq, Colombia, the carrier and conversion) are committed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is moderate: the issuer competes with other floating terminal owners, LNG sellers and LNG-to-power developers, and awards turn on experience, delivery speed and price. Entry is possible: the annual report notes limited availability of floating terminals in recent years but expects state-sponsored entities and major energy companies may buy, build or convert terminals, which would pressure rates on new and renewed contracts. The filings do not rank substitutes; the issuer's own example is gas displacing coal in Pakistan and Bangladesh. Buyer power is high because customers are few and state-linked, offset by take-or-pay terms and early-termination fees. Supplier power is high for LNG supply, as the Qatar force majeure shows, and for shipyard capacity, which drives the delivery dates of new terminals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors are a primary driver here: the Middle East conflict, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and sovereign counterparties directly changed the Iraq timetable, Qatar supply and the Colombia plan. Economic factors matter through LNG prices (the Dutch gas benchmark averaged USD 17.62 per MMBtu and the Japan-Korea benchmark USD 19.77 in the third quarter, up from USD 15.61 and USD 17.65 in the second) and foreign currency fluctuations, which the annual report names as a risk. Social and technological factors are secondary; the planned reliquefaction unit on one terminal is an operating improvement, not a credit driver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are the contracts, a redeployable fleet and a record of extensions; weaknesses are customer concentration, negative free cash flow and structural subordination. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the Iraq, Colombia and Bahamas contracts and the conversion project, which add contracted earnings from 2027 and 2028, while the Sequoia extension through 2038 lengthens an existing contract. Threats are prolonged conflict, force majeure turning into termination, counterparty payment delay and any loosening of creditor protections through further amendments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Main supports are contracted income, moderate leverage and a long-dated debt profile; constraints are weak free cash flow, concentration and structure; the trend is leverage rising from net cash while cash falls; the key missing data are covenant headroom, contract expiries and the cost of the carrier and conversion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F01; calculation F05; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over twelve to twenty-four months tailwinds are the Colombia charter and Bahamas deliveries from the first quarter of 2027 and the Iraq start in the second quarter of 2027; headwinds are the Gulf conflict, the Qatar force majeure, the end of the nine-month Jordan charter that began in July 2026 unless it is extended, the carrier remainder due in the first quarter of 2027 and the conversion spending. Global LNG trade held up at about 101 million tonnes in the third quarter of 2026 against 106 in the third quarter of 2025, so import demand is resilient but supply is tight. Over three to five years the credit events are the 2029 revolver maturity and the May 2030 notes. Sector headwinds are price volatility and state counterparties; company headwinds are covenant uncertainty and control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: An issuer-specific downside begins with the Gulf conflict continuing past the revised dates: the Iraq terminal slips again and Qatar supply stays under force majeure, interrupting LNG sales to Bangladesh. First break: LNG, gas and power margins and operating cash flow fall while committed growth spending on the carrier and conversion continues. Financial transmission: free cash flow stays negative, cash declines and the company draws the revolver, which lifts net leverage from 1.53x. Refinancing: the notes mature in May 2030 and a weaker leverage position raises refinancing cost, while distributions are gated at 3.25x leverage. Management levers are deferring growth spending, suspending buybacks and distributions and extending contracts; resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in the next twelve months because maintenance spending is small, but not shown beyond that. Observable triggers are quarterly operating cash flow, revolver drawings and customer payment timing; no numerical stress is established.

Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market conditions in 2030, when most principal falls due, and on whether the Iraq and Colombia contracts start on time. The primary downside path is continued Gulf disruption delaying contracted earnings while growth spending drains cash. Further analysis would require executed debt documents, covenant compliance figures, contract expiries and the cost of the carrier and conversion. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: deployment delay and negative free cash flow.
